original_card.question: Can one uncovered interface implication be formalized with exact caller and certificate bindings?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one missing statement with quantified hypotheses, actual caller and existing coverage. A compact-switch lemma is a candidate only after its mathematical contract is reviewed. Establish a bounded proof plan before a separately budgeted proof-assistant build; do not rerun large Lean jobs as orientation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

existing_checks.remaining: Exact theorem-to-caller binding and genuinely uncovered interface lemmas.
Uniform algorithmic implications, not another endpoint digit.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: compact-switch formalization proposed as future validation.
existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Independent audit of Nick Petalas's PR #6038 (research/conjugate-pair-every-group, head 0cee0e104b68ce6f06bf84af03f46ac30680e64c): line-by-line check of its written all-group four-call theorem; a stronger written theorem (Theorem S: any label set avoiding the two target entries, any coincidences, any field, r >= 2) with a two-case proof; and a group-free finite certificate over small prime fields and widths.
scope_change_reason: The chooser drew independent-verification. independent-moment on the selected #6030 word already has two audits (maintainer review and #6043), and no open PR claims a higher kappa. #6038 is a fresh unreviewed all-group theorem that answers #4089's open question 2. Its finite check depends on coincidence keys from five named groups. An independent proof check plus a check free of group-specific inputs is the missing implication for that claim. formal-interface-lemma is the closest card: this binds a theorem to a certificate, without a proof-assistant build.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the BIT register-model line. It confirms that the conjugate-pair alphabet offers no call saving in any group. Theorem S extends this to every label set that avoids the target entries, so a nonabelian-alphabet BIT proposal must find its gain elsewhere. No kappa effect.
stop_rule: Stop at the first error in #6038's proof or the first relaxed solution at length <= 3; otherwise stop after the written strengthening and the registered finite tiers.
evidence: PROOF.md (Theorem S, two-case proof); README audit notes on #6038 PROOF.md; verify.py, a stdlib group-free relaxation over r,q = (2,2),(2,3),(2,5),(3,2) with full and singleton tiers and positive/negative controls; local run at (2,7).
author: Josie Elliston
ai_assistance: Claude (Anthropic) assisted with the audit, the proof, the code and the writing. An OpenAI Codex read-only adversarial review of #6038's PROOF.md and of verify.py reported no error.

open_questions.question: Is there a uniform floor of 6 calls for diag([g],[h]) when neither entry is a product of at most two labels, e.g. diag([xyx],[yxy])? (#6038 open question 1)
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would replace per-group pair censuses with one uniform argument.
open_questions.first_step: The support-only analogue of Theorem S fails. A local probe at r=2 over F2, with only size>=3 subsets allowed to carry g or h, finds relaxed solutions at length 4 (20/1296 tuples) and 5 (938/7776). Next, add the label relations: a full-tier table for labels {x,y} and target (xyx, yxy), then test whether those length-4 solutions survive.
open_questions.blocked_by: Sound single-equation rules for the hypothesis xyx != yxy; the commutation rule used here does not imply it.

open_questions.question: Formalize Theorem S in a proof assistant.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is a short statement about rank-one matrices over a field and would give a kernel-checked floor.
open_questions.first_step: State the three class equations and the corner rules for k = 3 over an arbitrary field.
